title: Verstappen wins in Las Vegas for third time in four years
extract: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finished second and third, while George Russell hit the barriers late and Ferrari teammates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided.

title: Ferrari adds 296 Challenge Evo and Stradale variants
extract: Motorsport.com reports two new additions to the 296 Challenge family: an Evo track variant and a road-going Stradale version. The pairing extends Ferrari's V6 platform in both competition and road-car directions.

title: Linux 7.4 to remove NVMe namespaces in parallel for faster results
extract: A change merged for Linux 7.4 removes NVMe namespaces asynchronously rather than serially, allowing grace-period waits to overlap. The optimization can substantially shorten disconnect times for controllers with many namespaces.

title: Sashiko AI introduces Linux performance specialist review stage
extract: The open-source Sashiko AI code-review tool adds an optional performance-specialist stage for Linux kernel patches. Phoronix reports its benchmark's positive detection rate rising from 15% to 70%, without adding false positives on neutral commits.

title: AWS got hit by an outage too. Here's why you didn't hear about it
extract: Corey Quinn examines a November 15 us-east-1 incident that disrupted sign-up, authentication and connectivity, while AWS's status page lagged customer reports by 93 minutes. A useful look at the gap between service health and customer-visible incident reporting.

title: KDE Plasma 6.9 allows adjusting the text cursor blinking rate, other improvements
extract: The upcoming Plasma 6.9 adds control over text-cursor blinking, improved Chinese, Japanese and Korean input on the on-screen keyboard, more targeted multi-display settings and faster screenshots. KWin also gains NVIDIA overlay-plane support.

title: NASA Mars rover and orbiter suffer glitches
extract: Perseverance has paused science operations because of a communications-rate problem, while the long-running Mars Odyssey orbiter faces a more serious anomaly that could threaten its mission. Odyssey has now operated for roughly a quarter-century.

title: Amazon's split personality: AWS embraces bot commerce while main site enforces bans
extract: AWS Marketplace is opening agentic purchasing through x402 and Bedrock AgentCore Payments, even as Amazon's retail site blocks third-party shopping bots. The split highlights how quickly agent commerce is becoming a platform feature.

title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
extract: PHP's annual release introduces more security-friendly defaults for session handling. It arrives alongside coordinated patched releases across supported branches that close seven critical remote-code-execution flaws.

title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
extract: Researchers found no card numbers, passwords or home addresses in leaked Visa and Mastercard files, but did find mobile numbers, BIN prefixes and travel, hotel and restaurant bookings that could support convincing phishing. The published sample is only a small fraction of the data thieves claim to hold.

title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
extract: Signal now blocks operating-system AI agents such as Siri and Gemini from capturing message screens by default, unless users explicitly allow it. The change responds to concerns that on-screen AI features could expose private conversations to external services.

title: Nvidia’s journey to forge the one CPU SKU to rule them all
extract: Nvidia is pitching Vera as a single 88-core, 3.3GHz Arm CPU design for most datacentre workloads, from Vera-Rubin systems to standalone HPC racks. The deep dive explains how it aims to balance throughput and latency rather than offer dozens of narrowly tuned SKUs.

title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
extract: Amazon says suspected China-linked attackers used the open-source Cairn framework to find and exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label, gaining control of a university server. The agents adapted over many hours with little human direction.

title: Dutch data watchdog highlights safety issues with AI glasses
extract: A Dutch regulator tested six smart-glasses models and found failures involving medication instructions, child-safety warnings and even a false claim that emergency services had been called during a CPR simulation. It advised consumers against buying them for now.

title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
extract: The Global Electronics Association warns that AI-server demand is squeezing PCB materials and fabrication capacity, crowding out automotive, medical, industrial and defence orders. It says meaningful relief may not arrive before mid-2028.

title: Spy court blasts UK secrecy, forces government to admit Apple ‘backdoor’ demand
extract: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal has confirmed that the UK government served Apple with a Technical Capability Notice, while its precise demands remain secret. The ruling renews scrutiny of the government's pressure over end-to-end encrypted iCloud data.

title: Windows 11 passkey bug cries failure after successful sign-in
extract: A cross-device passkey bug could show Android users a failed-authentication message even after the Windows 11 PC sign-in succeeded. Microsoft included a fix in optional update KB5132057 for versions 25H2 and 26H2.

title: vAmigaWeb emulator gains lower audio latency and a Kickstart replacement
extract: The browser-based Amiga emulator moves to vAmigaCore 5.0, improving super-hires pixel accuracy and reducing audio latency. It also offers KickSlopStart, a free Kickstart 1.3-compatible replacement for classic A500 and A2000 setups.

title: FireFront brings top-down tank action to RTG Amigas
extract: FireFront is a top-down Amiga tank game inspired by Fire Power, with a ten-mission campaign, three selectable tanks and rescue or destruction objectives. It requires at least a 68030 CPU and RTG graphics.

title: Copper Basic 1.3 adds an Amiga BASIC cross-compiler
extract: Copper Basic 1.3 is a Python cross-compiler that produces bootable A500-compatible disk images and adds commands for Amiga custom chips. Amiga News notes that the advertised source archives are empty, so the project's source is not currently inspectable.

title: PiAROS 0.5 released for Raspberry Pi
extract: PiAROS 0.5 is a 64-bit AROS distribution for Raspberry Pi 3, Pi 4/400 and Pi 5/500, accompanied by a new project website.

title: CrylicEdit 1.4 adds UTF support and macros
extract: CrylicEdit 1.4 adds UTF-8 and UTF-16 reading, UTF-8 writing, macros and word wrapping while retaining compatibility with Amiga systems from a 1MB Amiga 500 through RTG-equipped machines.

title: ChatGPT shrunk down to run on a Super Nintendo
extract: Retro tech journalist Benj Edwards has distilled a 2.2-million-parameter language model into an SNES ROM, with an optional tiny Wikipedia factbook; a related NES ROM simulates talking to a ghost. It is a playful vintage-hardware experiment, not a useful general chatbot.

title: Green Kingdom by Ben Dark review – a luscious natural history of plant life
extract: Ben Dark traces the evolution of plant dynasties from ancient pond life to modern flowering species, blending botany, folklore and natural history. The review praises its vivid prose and connections between plant evolution, history and landscape.

title: From I Am Helen to You Can See Everything: the week in rave reviews
extract: The Guardian's weekly culture roundup highlights Honey, a Killing Eve prequel following a young female spy in 1980s Berlin, and The Altruists, a drama about FTX founders Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison. It also covers the documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes.

title: Ben Whishaw and Kathryn Hunter are a dynamite duo on the road to nowhere in Eurotrash
extract: The Young Vic adapts Christian Kracht's darkly comic novel into a road-trip play about a mother and son trying to give away questionable family money. The review praises the leads' chemistry and comic set-pieces while noting that the adaptation softens the novel's confrontation with Nazi family history.
